text.tspan: Tectonic Puzzle - Minor Tectonic Plate Pieces (1:1 scale)
Tectonic Puzzle - Major Tectonic Plate Pieces (1:2 scale)
Tectonic Puzzle - Assembling the Earth's Interior
Contains tectonic plate information from Hugo Ahlenius' World tectonic plates and boundaries repository (https://github.com/fraxen/
tectonicplates.git), which is made available under the Open Data Commons Attribution license. Contains heightmap information based on
GEBCO 2020 Grid and preprocessed by Sean Bradley (https://sbcode.net/topoearth/gebco-heightmap-5400x2700/#license). Contains colour
information based on the specular texture map of Earth from Solar System Scope (https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/). Contains
Moho depth information from the GEMMA crustal model. D. Sampietro, M. Reguzzoni, M. Negretti (2013). The GEMMA crustal model: first
validation and data distribution. In: Proceedings of the ESA Living Planet Symposium, 9-13 September 2013, Edinburgh (UK), ESA SP-722

text.inkscape:label: inner core description
text.tspan: The Earth's solid inner core (yellow) is a solid ball 2442km across, made of a
mixture of iron and nickel. Its surface is over 5000 °C, as hot as the surface of

text.inkscape:label: outer core description
text.tspan: The Earth's liquid outer core (orange) is mostly made of melted iron and nickel.
Electric currents in the core produce the Earth's magnetic field, which protects
us from space radiation and makes compasses work, however this puzzle
doesn't have magnets in the outer core to allow the parts to move around more
like a liquid! The outer core is 2260km thick and reaches a heat of 3700-7700 °C

text.inkscape:label: mantle description
text.tspan: The Earth's rocky mantle (red) is mostly solid, but due to the heat and pressure
it can flow over time, allowing convection, where plumes of hotter material rise
from the bottom, and cooler material sinks from the top. The mantle is 2900km
thick, and reaches a heat of about 3900 °C at the bottom.

text.inkscape:label: moho description
text.tspan: The Moho (Mohorovičić discontinuity) is the boundary
between the lighter crust (grey) and heavier mantle
The tectonic plate pieces in this puzzle go a little
deeper than the Moho, but the red bottom surfaces
(and matching surfaces of the mantle pieces) follow
the approximate shape of the Moho (with depth

text.inkscape:label: crust description
text.tspan: The Earth's rocky crust (grey) is broken into tectonic
plates which "float" on the mantle (red), like a giant jigsaw
puzzle. In this puzzle they are separated by deep trenches,
but that's just so you can see them. The crust gets hotter
with depth, reaching 700-1600 °C at the bottom.

text.inkscape:label: crust thickness
text.tspan: Notice how the oceanic crust under the sea is generally
thinner (5-10km) than continental crust under land (25-70km).

text.inkscape:label: longitude latitude
text.tspan: the surface to sea level so
you can see where the sea

text.inkscape:label: vertical exaggeration
text.tspan: The height of land (green) and depth of seabed
from sea level. This makes mountain ranges,
ocean depths and the crust (grey) visible.
The real Earth is much smoother!
